Colour key used throughout Module 7: blue = pretrained weights, grey = random or untrained weights, orange = task-specific head, green = data. Takeaway: a pretrained model's value is in its learned numbers, not its structure.

> 🖼 *IMAGE 7.1.2 — The Lifecycle of a Pretrained Model.* A left-to-right flow diagram on a white background with four stages connected by thick arrows. Stage 1 (green): a stack of book and web-page icons labelled "Unlabelled text: books, web pages". Arrow labelled "pretraining: guess the [MASK]ed word". Stage 2 (blue): a tall rounded rectangle with six blue layers and a small grey-blue head labelled "masked-word head", titled "Base model (distilbert-base-uncased)". Arrow labelled "fine-tuning on a small labelled dataset (SST-2)", with a small green card stack beneath it labelled "short film-review sentences, positive/negative". Stage 3: the same blue body with a small orange head labelled "sentiment head (2 outputs)", titled "Adapted model (…-finetuned-sst-2-english)". Arrow labelled "downstream use". Stage 4: a speech-bubble card "A wonderful film with a brilliant cast." → "POSITIVE 1.000". Above stages 1–2, a bracket labelled "done once, by a lab, at great cost"; above stages 3–4, a bracket labelled "done by everyone else, cheaply". Takeaway: pretraining is expensive and done once; adaptation and use are cheap and done many times.

> 🖼 *IMAGE 7.1.3 — One Body, Many Heads.* On a white background, a single large blue rounded rectangle in the centre labelled "pretrained DistilBERT body · 6 layers · shared by every task". From its top edge, four thin lines fan out to four small orange boxes arranged in an arc: "masked-word head → guess hidden words", "classification head → positive / negative", "question-answering head → answer start & end", "token-labelling head → tag each word". Each orange box has a tiny example card beside it: "The movie was absolutely [MASK]. → fantastic", "A wonderful film… → POSITIVE", "Where is the Eiffel Tower? → [Paris]", "Ada lived in London → PERSON · · PLACE". A small grey note under three of the heads: "new head: random until trained". Takeaway: a foundation model is one expensive shared body plus cheap task-specific heads.

> 🖼 *IMAGE 7.1.4 — What You Download.* A folder icon on a white background labelled "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english / snapshot 714eb0fa89d2…". Inside, three file cards in a row. Card 1, small, labelled "config.json · the blueprint" with three bullet lines: "6 layers, 12 heads, width 768", "vocabulary 30,522", "labels: 0 = NEGATIVE, 1 = POSITIVE". Card 2, very large and blue, labelled "model.safetensors · the knowledge · 267.8 MB" with a bar inside it divided into three segments of proportional width: "embeddings 35.6%", "6 Transformer layers 63.5%", and a thin orange sliver "head 0.9%". Card 3, small, labelled "tokenizer files · the vocabulary" with "vocab.txt, tokenizer.json". Under the folder, a grey box labelled "Transformers library (on your computer) · the code that assembles these into a working model". Takeaway: a pretrained model is a blueprint plus a large file of numbers; the code comes from the library.

> 🖼 *IMAGE 7.1.5 — The Pretrained-Model Picture.* A single summary diagram on a white background, read left to right. Left, in green: "Unlabelled text → pretraining (guess hidden words)". Centre, in blue: a large rounded rectangle "Base model: config.json + model.safetensors", with three small callouts: "learns grammar ✓", "builds contextual meaning ✓ (bank ≠ bank)", "facts: unreliable ✗". Right: three orange heads attached to copies of the blue body, labelled "sentiment", "question answering", "token labels", with the caption "one body, many tasks". Bottom strip: a small bar chart with four bars labelled "random weights 0.486", "pretrained, 0 labels 0.874", "TF-IDF, 1,000 labels 0.826", "TF-IDF, 22,404 labels 0.918", with a note "pretrained wins when labels are scarce; adapt it when they aren't". Takeaway: pretrained weights are a powerful, free starting point, to be measured and, when needed, adapted.

> 🖼 *IMAGE 8.3.2 — Where the Bar Is.* A horizontal number line on a white background from 0.45 to 0.95 labelled "test accuracy (1,000 reviews)", with markers: grey "always negative 0.485", green "TF-IDF, 1,000 labels 0.828", blue "frozen DistilBERT + head 0.837", orange "SST-2 off the shelf 0.873" (drawn as a tall bar labelled "the bar for 1,000 labels"), and dark green "TF-IDF, all labels 0.913". Above the line, two dashed empty markers labelled "8.4 full fine-tuning ?" and "8.5 LoRA ?". Under the line, a bracket from 0.828 to 0.837 labelled "not significantly different (p = 0.56)". Takeaway: an adapted model trained on 1,000 labels must beat 0.873 to justify itself.
